claims.text: Preferential diffusion and oxidation of Si, Mn, or Al at the surface governs whether CrFeCoNiX alloys form coherent, low-stress protective oxide scales above 900 °C.
Beneficial segregation of X promotes formation of a continuous spinel or other oxide phase.
The resulting protective oxide has a close lattice match to the underlying alloy.
Close lattice matching minimizes oxide-scale stress and prevents cracking or spallation.
The proposed behavior applies to CrFeCoNiX alloys in either single-phase or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
A coherent spinel, Al2O3-rich layer, or SiO2-rich layer can act as the protective structural mediator.
The protective oxide scale is well lattice-matched with the alloy substrate.
Si, Mn, or Al has higher oxygen affinity and suitable diffusivity relative to the other alloy constituents.
During high-temperature exposure, X segregates to the surface and reacts to form a stable oxide.
Crystallographic compatibility and low growth-induced stress cause the oxide to adhere coherently to the substrate.
Uniform enrichment of X across the phases of a multiphase alloy is critical for protective-scale stability.
Nonuniform X enrichment creates microstructural mismatches that increase local stress and lead to oxide spallation.
Alloys with appropriate X content and homogeneous X distribution will form more uniform, adherent, and stable oxide scales than alloys lacking beneficial X segregation.
Appropriate X content and distribution will reduce oxide cracking and spallation.
Appropriate X content and distribution will reduce further oxidation and corrosive attack.
CrFeCoNi without X, or with insufficient X segregation, forms less coherent and higher-stress oxide scales prone to cracking and spallation.
The mechanism is applicable above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
The mechanism may not apply at significantly lower temperatures or in fundamentally different alloy systems.
The oxide phase and degree of spallation improvement depend on X identity, X concentration, and its microstructural distribution.
